RTS-RPGs are not really that common, at least not those who operate in real time.

If you'd like a bit of an alternative, try Sacrifice. It's essentially a mix of RPG and RTS in which you control a sorcerer via third-person camera and summon all kinds of minions while fighting enemy sorcerer. Very unique artstyle, but also a bit antiquated.

I think it depends a lot on what you like about XCOM that you are looking for? It sounds like you just enjoy the character growth in a stable of soldiers? But the slow, turn based, thoughtful tactics aren't doing it for you.

The thing about turn based tactical games is they have very deep roots. XCom, Jagged Alliance and others go back almost to the dawn of the DOS platform. The thing about trying to play these games in real time is that it's easy for characters to get killed. And since character grown and permadeath is such a huge mechanic, it just makes real time frustrating. As you said happened in Fallout Tactics.

Now, all that being said, there might be a few games up your alley.

Icewind Dale was a pretty straight up tactical combat game based on Advanced Dungeons & Dragons 2nd Edition. Compared to Baldur's Gate or Planescape: Torment, the role playing elements are light. Most obviously, you roll up all 6 characters you'll be using the rest of the game up front, instead of starting with one character and recruiting the rest inside the game. The game still uses a pause system (just hit spacebar), and you'll need to use it, but the core of the game is real time, and the tactics are fun.

You may find Syndicate up your alley? I haven't played it personally, but I believe it's real time, and you upgrade your 4 man corporate hit squad throughout the game.
Satellite Reign is the spiritual successor to the Syndicate series, if people need something less 90s graphics.

The issue is that that style of play fits turn based much better then realtime. The gap between turnbased and RTS isn't really filled by much. Some give you an option to upgrade hero units between fights or when they level like Warcraft 3 but that is about the best I can think of. Some of the Warhammer 40k games may have that feature as well but I'm not sure on that been a while, though they were more use what you have and micromanage then just throw them at things and rebuild then most RTS games out there.

If you are looking for something like XCOM, but real time with pause, then go with UFO: Aftermath, UFO: Afterlight or UFO: Aftershock.

Arcanum is an excellent RPG and has either real time combat or turn based. You can change between them with a menu setting at will.
